modes.title: Run on any image: a file, a URL or bytes
modes.description: Send the image itself with one prompt - a phrase, a box or points - and the objects come back. Nothing is saved: no dataset, no image, no annotation.

inputs.note: The CLI and Python read it; over HTTP it is the multipart `file`.
The CLI and Python fetch it on your machine, then upload it (pictograph 1.69.107 or newer). Over HTTP, download it and send the bytes.
Python (`image=<bytes>`), HTTP (multipart `file`), and the CLI: `-` reads the image from stdin (pictograph 1.69.107 or newer).

The CLI: `--video clip.mp4 --sample-fps 2` decodes it on your machine (OpenCV: `pip install "pictograph[inference]"`) and runs the frames a workflow over the same file would sample, one JSON line per frame with its `frame` index and `t` (seconds). Each frame is one call and one image charged (pictograph 1.69.107 or newer); for a long video a workflow reads it on Pictograph.

The CLI: `--dataset my-dataset [--directory /val] [--limit N]` reads one of your datasets' images and prints predictions, one JSON line per image with its address and `image_id`; it writes nothing (a dataset in cold storage must be restored first) (pictograph 1.69.107 or newer). The text, box and point modes run on one dataset image without downloading it.

limits.note: One image up to 25 MB and 50 megapixels (JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, TIFF), and one prompt per call: `text`, `box` or `point`. The first call after a quiet spell starts a GPU and can take a minute or two. The CLI takes several images at once (paths, globs, URLs) and prints one JSON line per image, `{"input", "result"}` or `{"input", "error"}` (pictograph 1.69.107 or newer).

requires: An API key with the member role or higher.

cost.summary: $0.01 per image (the same bytes are the same image), charged once when a prompt on that image completes. More prompts on the same image are free; a prompt that fails is free.

modes.returns: `{status, prompt, annotations, score, width, height, image_sha256, confidence_threshold, degraded, inference_time}` - nothing is saved. `width` and `height` are the upright image's (EXIF orientation applied), the space every coordinate is in. Over HTTP it is wrapped as `{"data": {...}}`.

model/Shelf Detector.summary: An object detection model (RF-DETR Nano) that predicts bottle, can, box, scoring 61.0% mAP.

parameters.name: confidence
parameters.description: Minimum score a prediction needs to be returned. Lower it to see more (and less certain) predictions. Hosted accepts 0.05-0.95 (`confidence_threshold` over HTTP); local accepts 0-1.

output.description: One annotation per detected object: `name` is the class, `bounding_box` is `{x, y, w, h}` with (x, y) the top-left corner, `confidence` is 0-1.
output.coordinates: Absolute pixels of the image you sent, origin at the top-left, x to the right and y down. Nothing is normalized to 0-1.

BoundingBox.description: Top-left + width/height bounding box. ``w`` and ``h`` strictly positive.
BoundingBox.title: BoundingBox

OrientedBoxGeometry.description:
Oriented (rotated) bounding box - centre, extents, and a rotation (B97).

``angle`` is DEGREES, clockwise-positive in image space (x → right, y → DOWN),
the same convention CVAT's ``rotation`` uses. ``w``/``h`` are the box's extents
along its OWN axes, so they do not change when it is turned.
OrientedBoxGeometry.title: OrientedBoxGeometry

schema.description:
A bounding box. A ROTATED box is this same type carrying an optional
``oriented_box`` attribute - an oriented box is a special case of a bounding box,
not its own annotation type. ``bounding_box`` is always the axis-aligned enclosure
(what training and every OBB-unaware consumer reads); ``oriented_box`` is present
only on a rotated box and is read by consumers with an OBB export pipeline
(YOLO-OBB / DOTA). A plain box carries no oriented metadata.

name.description: Class label; must match a dataset class.
name.title: Name

oriented_box.description: Optional. Present only on a rotated box: the parametric oriented box (cx, cy, w, h, angle in degrees). `bounding_box` is derived from it (its axis-aligned enclosure) on save. Pictograph does not train OBB - a box trains on its orthogonal `bounding_box` whether or not it is rotated.

modes.title: Run one image on Pictograph (nothing to install)
modes.description: Uploads one image and returns its predictions. Runs on Pictograph's CPU inference service, so the first call after a quiet spell takes a few seconds longer while it starts.

inputs.note: The CLI and Python fetch it on your machine, then upload it (pictograph 1.69.99 or newer). Over HTTP, download it and send the bytes.
Python (`image=<bytes>`), HTTP (multipart `file`), and the CLI: `-` reads the image from stdin (pictograph 1.69.99 or newer).

The CLI: `--video clip.mp4 --sample-fps 2` decodes it on your machine (OpenCV: `pip install "pictograph[inference]"`) and runs the frames a workflow over the same file would sample, one JSON line per frame with its `frame` index and `t` (seconds), each frame one hosted call (pictograph 1.69.102 or newer). Frames spend the shared daily capacity: run locally for a long video, or run a workflow, which reads video on Pictograph.

The CLI: `--dataset my-dataset [--directory /val] [--limit N]` reads one of your datasets' images and prints predictions, one JSON line per image with its address and `image_id`; it writes nothing (a dataset in cold storage must be restored first), each image one hosted call (pictograph 1.69.102 or newer); run locally for volume. To SAVE predictions as draft labels use the dataset mode.

limits.note: One image up to 25 MB and 50 megapixels. Capacity is shared across all users each day: a 429 with Retry-After means it is spent - run the model locally instead. The CLI takes several images at once (paths, globs like 'frames/*.jpg', URLs) and prints one JSON line per image, `{"input", "result"}` or `{"input", "error"}` (pictograph 1.69.99 or newer).

requires: An API key with the member role or higher.

To SAVE predictions as draft labels use the dataset mode.

modes.title: Call the endpoint
modes.description: Sends one image to the deployment's own URL. Authenticated by the deployment's `pk_deploy_` token alone - no account API key needed.

inputs.note: The CLI and Python fetch it; over HTTP send `{"image": {"type": "url", "value": ...}}` and the endpoint fetches it.
HTTP: multipart `file`, or JSON `{"image": {"type": "base64", "value": ...}}`. Python: `infer(<bytes>)`. CLI: `-` reads the image from stdin (pictograph 1.69.99 or newer).

The CLI: `--video clip.mp4 --sample-fps 2` decodes it on your machine (OpenCV: `pip install "pictograph[inference]"`) and runs the frames a workflow over the same file would sample, one JSON line per frame with its `frame` index and `t` (seconds), each frame sent as a JPEG (pictograph 1.69.102 or newer). The token alone is enough.

The CLI: `--dataset my-dataset [--directory /val] [--limit N]` reads one of your datasets' images and prints predictions, one JSON line per image with its address and `image_id`; it writes nothing (a dataset in cold storage must be restored first), each image one call (pictograph 1.69.102 or newer). Reading the dataset also needs an account API key.

limits.note: One image per call. The CLI takes several images at once (paths, globs like 'frames/*.jpg', URLs) and prints one JSON line per image, `{"input", "result"}` or `{"input", "error"}` (pictograph 1.69.99 or newer).

requires: The deployment's token (pk_deploy_...). It was shown once when the deployment was created and can be shown again from its settings in the app.
Status `active`. A paused deployment answers 409: resume it first.

cost.summary: Billed for uptime, not per call: $0.0709 per minute while a container is up. It scales to zero when idle, so an unused endpoint costs nothing and the first call after it sleeps waits for a container to start (10 - 15 s).

modes.returns: `{model_type, predictions}`: `predictions` is the list of annotations described under Output.

import os

from pictograph import DeploymentClient

endpoint = DeploymentClient(
    endpoint="https://workflows.pictograph.io/d-abc123/predict",
    api_key=os.environ["PICTOGRAPH_DEPLOY_TOKEN"],
    task="object_detection",
)
result = endpoint.infer("photo.jpg")

workflow/Door counter.summary: A workflow that runs Shelf Detector + SAM3, tracks each object across frames, times dwell in zones and counts line crossings. Outputs: json, annotated_video.
workflow/Door counter.about: Counts people through the shop door.

parameters.name: sample_fps
parameters.description: Frames per second to sample from a video given as a storage URI or a link (`--video gs://...`, `--video https://...`). A local file uses the workflow's own setting.

output.description: Per-frame detections go to the outputs the graph names (json, annotated_video); each measure reports an aggregate, a time series and per-track values in `step_results`.
output.coordinates: Absolute pixels of the image you sent, origin at the top-left, x to the right and y down. Nothing is normalized to 0-1.

modes.title: Run it on a video or image on this machine
modes.description: Uploads it (a file, or bytes piped in) to your organization's storage, runs the workflow over it and waits for the result.

inputs.note: A video or an image on disk.
Use the url mode: Pictograph downloads it, nothing passes through your machine.
Python `source=<bytes>`, or the CLI's `--file -` from stdin (pictograph 1.69.108 or newer). Whether it is a video or an image is read from the bytes.
The whole point: frames are sampled, tracked and measured in order.
Use the dataset mode.

limits.note: A run is stopped after 1 hour.

requires: An API key with the member role or higher.
A graph with no validation errors.

cost.summary: $0.0709 a minute while a run or a stream holds one of its endpoint's containers (T4, US East): from the container's start until 60 s after the last run or stream on it ends, a failed run too - billed as uptime, like a deployment. A SAM3 block's GPU time is charged with its run.

modes.returns: A run record: `status`, `step_results` (each measure's totals, a time series and per-track values), `artifacts` (each output file with a signed `download_url`), and `warnings` (any cap that was hit). `--no-wait` returns `run_id` + `status_url` to poll instead.

run.python:
from pathlib import Path

from pictograph import Client

client = Client()  # reads PICTOGRAPH_API_KEY
run = client.workflows.invoke("Door counter", source=Path("clip.mp4"), wait=True)
print(run.status, run.step_results)
